stories.title: Hodler's Digest: Liquid 'white hat' recovers 4,000 BTC, ETFs post best inflows of 2026
stories.summary: Cointelegraph's weekly Hodler's Digest recaps two major stories: purported white-hat hackers withdrew roughly 4,000 BTC from the Bitcoin sidechain Liquid, and Bitcoin ETFs logged their strongest weekly inflows of 2026. The roundup ties together security and market news from the week.
stories.whyItMatters: A single digest citing both a major sidechain security incident and record ETF inflows shows how security risk and institutional demand are both live forces in the market right now.
whatToWatch: Full coverage of the Liquid withdrawal and its resolution
Whether the ETF inflow pace continues into the next reporting week
questions: What specific funds or issuers drove the ETF inflow figure?
Is the 4,000 BTC figure consistent with later reporting on the Liquid incident?

sources.title: ‘White hats’ take 4000 BTC from Liquid, ETFs see best inflows of 2026: Hodler’s Digest

stories.title: Citi and DBS complete first weekend tokenized cross-border deposit transfer via Swift
stories.summary: Citi and DBS say they completed the first weekend tokenized cross-border deposit transaction routed over Swift's network. The transaction shows tokenized deposits can settle outside normal banking hours, when traditional rails are typically closed.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a concrete sign that major banks are moving tokenization from pilot talk to live settlement infrastructure, which affects how fast institutional money can move on-chain.
whatToWatch: Whether Citi and DBS expand the service beyond a pilot
Other banks following with weekend or off-hours tokenized settlement
questions: What asset or currency pair was involved?
Does this run on a public chain or a permissioned ledger?

sources.title: Citi, DBS complete first weekend tokenized cross-border deposit on Swift

stories.title: Harmony proposes shutting down its layer 1, migrating ONE token to Ethereum
stories.summary: Harmony has proposed winding down its own layer-1 blockchain and migrating its native ONE token to Ethereum. The proposal would end Harmony as an independent chain and fold its token economy into Ethereum's ecosystem.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a rare case of an established layer-1 network voluntarily shutting down, underscoring how hard it is for mid-tier chains to sustain independent activity and security.
whatToWatch: Community and validator vote on the proposal
Details of the migration mechanism and timeline for ONE holders
questions: What prompted the shutdown decision now?
How will existing Harmony dApps and liquidity migrate?

sources.title: Harmony proposes shutting down layer 1, migrating ONE to Ethereum

stories.title: Bitcoin sidechain Liquid pauses after purported white hats withdraw $320M in BTC
stories.summary: The Bitcoin sidechain Liquid paused operations after parties described as "white hat" hackers withdrew about $320 million worth of BTC. The withdrawal appears to be a defensive move rather than theft for profit, though the network is now paused while the situation is assessed.
stories.whyItMatters: A $320 million withdrawal from a major Bitcoin sidechain is a serious security event that raises questions about the safety of funds locked in sidechains and bridges.
whatToWatch: Whether Liquid resumes normal operations
Official confirmation of who withdrew the funds and why
Any return of funds to the network
questions: What vulnerability prompted the withdrawal?
Are user funds still fully backed while the network is paused?

sources.title: Bitcoin sidechain Liquid pauses after purported ‘white hats’ withdraw $320M in BTC

stories.title: Whitehat hacker holds $320M in drained Bitcoin until developers patch network flaw
stories.summary: A whitehat hacker is holding roughly $320 million in Bitcoin drained from a network, and says they will return it once developers prove they have fixed a serious flaw, according to CryptoSlate. The move is framed as pressure to force a security fix rather than as theft.
stories.whyItMatters: The episode shows a hacker using drained funds as leverage to force a fix, raising questions about incident response and trust when "white hat" claims aren't independently verified.
whatToWatch: Confirmation from developers that the flaw is patched
Whether the hacker returns the funds as promised
questions: Who is verifying the hacker's identity and intent?
What exactly is the 'fatal network flaw' being referenced?

sources.title: A whitehat hacker is holding $320 million in drained Bitcoin until developers prove they patched a fatal network flaw

stories.title: Coldcard third-wave attacker moves 45% of stolen Bitcoin
stories.summary: The attacker behind the third wave of the Coldcard hardware wallet breach has moved 45% of the Bitcoin stolen in that incident. Movement of funds often signals an attempt to launder or cash out proceeds.
stories.whyItMatters: Hardware wallets are marketed as a safer alternative to exchanges, so a breach affecting Coldcard users raises concern about self-custody security assumptions.
whatToWatch: Whether the remaining stolen funds move next
Any wallet or exchange freezing the moved funds
Coldcard's response on the underlying vulnerability
questions: How did the attacker initially gain access to affected wallets?
How many users were affected in this third wave?

sources.title: Coldcard third-wave attacker moves 45% of stolen Bitcoin

stories.title: Fomo overtakes Pump.fun in daily revenue on Solana
stories.summary: The Solana-based platform Fomo has surpassed Pump.fun in daily revenue, according to Cointelegraph. The shift suggests a change in where token-launch and trading activity is concentrating on Solana.
stories.whyItMatters: Pump.fun has been the dominant venue for speculative token launches on Solana, so a rival overtaking it in revenue signals shifting user activity and competitive pressure in that niche.
whatToWatch: Whether Fomo sustains its lead over multiple days
Pump.fun's response, if any, to the shift
questions: What is driving users to Fomo specifically?
Is the revenue lead driven by fees, volume, or a specific promotion?

sources.title: Fomo overtakes Pump.fun in daily revenue on Solana

stories.title: Coldcard hacker moves $7.7M, nearly half of third-wave Bitcoin haul
stories.summary: Decrypt reports the attacker behind the third wave of the Coldcard breach has moved $7.7 million in Bitcoin, close to half of the total stolen in that wave. This matches other reporting that roughly 45% of the stolen funds have moved.
stories.whyItMatters: Tracking where stolen funds move can help investigators and exchanges flag and potentially freeze proceeds, and signals the attacker may be preparing to cash out.
whatToWatch: Destination of the moved $7.7 million
Whether exchanges flag or freeze related wallets
Movement of the remaining stolen funds
questions: Has any of the moved Bitcoin reached an exchange?
What security failure allowed the third-wave theft?

sources.title: Coldcard Hacker Moves $7.7M, Nearly Half of Third-Wave Bitcoin Haul

stories.title: CZ's Kyrgyzstan visit shows state backing alone can't guarantee a stablecoin exit
stories.summary: CryptoSlate examines Binance founder CZ's visit to Kyrgyzstan in the context of a state-linked stablecoin project. The piece argues that government backing doesn't by itself guarantee holders can reliably exit or redeem the token.
stories.whyItMatters: State-affiliated stablecoins are being positioned as trustworthy by association with governments, so questions about actual redemption mechanics matter for anyone holding or evaluating them.
whatToWatch: Further details on the Kyrgyzstan stablecoin's redemption mechanism
Any regulatory or reserve disclosures tied to the project
questions: What specific stablecoin and reserve structure is involved?
What is CZ's formal role in the project, if any?

sources.title: CZ’s Kyrgyzstan visit highlights why state backing cannot guarantee a stablecoin exit

stories.title: Bitcoin ETF inflows fall 76% heading into Labor Day, with only BlackRock and Fidelity drawing fresh money
stories.summary: Bitcoin ETF inflows dropped 76% heading into the Labor Day break, according to CryptoSlate, with BlackRock and Fidelity the only issuers attracting net new money. Other issuers saw flat or negative flows over the period.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows are a key gauge of institutional demand for Bitcoin, so a sharp drop concentrated in just two issuers suggests broader institutional appetite may be cooling or consolidating.
whatToWatch: Whether inflows recover after the Labor Day break
Flow data for issuers beyond BlackRock and Fidelity in coming weeks
questions: Is the drop seasonal or a sign of a broader demand shift?
How do these flows compare to the same period last year?

sources.title: Bitcoin ETF inflows fall 76% entering Labor Day break as only BlackRock and Fidelity attract fresh money

stories.title: Purported white-hat hackers withdraw $320M in Bitcoin from Liquid
stories.summary: Decrypt reports that parties described as "purported white-hat hackers" withdrew $320 million in Bitcoin from the Liquid sidechain. The white-hat characterization is not independently confirmed, and the network has responded to the withdrawal.
stories.whyItMatters: A $320 million withdrawal from a Bitcoin sidechain, whatever the intent behind it, is a major security event that could affect confidence in sidechain custody.
whatToWatch: Independent confirmation of the withdrawers' identity and motive
Liquid's official statement and next steps
Whether funds are returned
questions: Who verified the 'white hat' framing?
What happens to user funds while this is unresolved?

sources.title: 'Purported White-Hat Hackers' Withdraw $320M in Bitcoin From Liquid

stories.title: Philippines considers freezing new payment operator registrations, tightening VASP checks
stories.summary: The Philippines is reportedly considering a freeze on new payment operator registrations alongside tighter checks on virtual asset service providers, according to Cointelegraph. The move would tighten oversight of crypto-related payment businesses in the country.
stories.whyItMatters: Tighter VASP registration rules in a major Southeast Asian crypto market could raise compliance costs and slow new entrants, affecting how easily crypto payment firms can operate there.
whatToWatch: Formal announcement or timeline from Philippine regulators
Reaction from existing registered payment operators and VASPs
questions: What triggered the proposed freeze?
Would existing registered operators be grandfathered in?

sources.title: Philippines eyes payment operator registration freeze, tighter VASP checks
